findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee wash and lather hands, then turn off the faucet before using paper towels. CORRECTED- education was provided. Review hand washing procedures with staff, a paper towel should be used to dry hands and THEN turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.

findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspector observed unwashed produce stored on the floor in the walk in cooler. Store foods at least 6 inches above the ground to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a to-go soup bowl submerged in the soy sauce. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) removed the bowl to be discarded, and replaced with a ladel. Education occurred regarding the need for a scoop with a handle to prevent potential bare hand contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The soap in the back hand washing sink was observed to be not properly dispensing. CORRECTED- a hand soap pump was brought to the hand washing sink. Ensure hand washing sinks are always supplied with accessible soap for proper hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: A total of four cans (a mixture of soy sauce and oyster sauce) were observed to contain dents along the seams. CORRECTED- The PIC voluntarily used post-it notes to mark the dented cans with a large “X” to be sent back to their supplier. The PIC stated the kitchen manager stocks the shelves, and communicated this new procedure to them. Ensure seams of cans are not dented to prevent the entry and growth of Botulism. Mark and move these cans aside in the future.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.

CORRECTED- Person in charge moved cloth to sanitizer bucket before inspector was able to discuss item. Ensure wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer buckets in between uses to prevent the growth and harborage of bacteria.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Soiled rice scoops and holder were left at the cook line/service area from the previous day of operation. Clean rice scoop and container were provided. PIC was advised to ensure soiled equipment is removed from service area and at minimum placed at 3 part sink at the end of operations to ensure soiled items are not potentially available for use the next day. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Prepared foods leftover from Sunday in the walk-in cooler did not have date marks, including but not limited to, white rice, sweet and sour chicken, and General Tso chicken. Thawed shrimp eggrolls and portion of sweet and sour chicken in the reach-in cooler were also without date marks. Foods were properly dated during inspection and kept for use. Date marking and options for tracking dates (piece of notebook paper posted on cooler, etc.) were discussed.
A Refrigerated, ready to eat, TCS food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41F/below for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. If products are frozen, then dates need to be changed and documented accordingly to reflect proper time frame for use and ensure the foods are used or discarded within a total of 7 days.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Open #10 can of Ketchup from Sunday was observed in the bottom of the prep cooler. Proper storage was discussed. Acidic foods need to be stored in plastic or stainless steel containers after opening if they will not be used within the current operating day. Inner lining of cans may corrode off into foods when acidic foods are left inside the original can after opening. Ketchup and Hoisin sauce were were placed in stainless steel containers during inspection.
Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Owner with food manager certification was not at the facility upon arrival of inspector. Cooks have expired food handler certifications. PIC was contacted by husband and arrived within ~10 minutes of inspectors arrival. PIC was advised as to the need for a certified food manager to be present during all hours of operation, including morning prep.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Quarter pan of sauce was stacked on a pan of mushrooms in the top holding area of the prep cooler. A barrier was not present between the bottom of the pan and the mushrooms in the pan beneath. Proper storage with barriers between stacked pans of food was discussed. The bottoms of pans are not considered clean surfaces once they are in use and should not stored in direct contact with unwrapped foods. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11 Rice scoops and container were washed, rinsed, and then quickly dunked in sanitizer solution prior to PIC starting to remove items to air dry. Also, large mixing bowls with rinse and bleach solutions were setup in the second and third compartments of the 3 part sink rather than using the compartments, and wash step was completed without the use of the first basin, which had soiled dishes in it. Proper setup and use of the 3 part sink was discussed, with emphasis on the ability to properly submerge items during sanitize step and allow for a contact time of at least 10 seconds. Scoop and holder were placed in bleach solution for ~1 minute prior to removing to air dry. 
After being cleaned, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in chemical manual operations, including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114 (in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions). Contact time shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use instructions by providing at least 10 seconds for chlorine chemical sanitizing solutions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Soiled bowl, tongs, and rice scoops were left at the cook line/service area from the previous day of operation. Bowl and tongs were replaced with clean equipment and rice scoops were cleaned and sanitized for lunch service. PIC was advised to ensure soiled equipment is removed from service area and at minimum placed at 3 part sink at the end of operations to ensure soiled items are not potentially available for use the next day. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Colander of thawing shrimp was observed in the back prep sink under cold running water. Water was in direct contact with only a small portion of the product and did not allow for complete submersion in water. If time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food is thawed under cold running water it must meet the requirements of FDA Food Code Section 3-501.13(B), and product needs to be completely submerged during the thawing process. PIC was advised to provide a storage container within the sink or another means to allow for thawing foods to be submerged in cold water as it is running over the product.
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled

Soiled linens shall be kept in clean, nonabsorbent receptacles or clean, washable laundry bags and stored and transported to prevent contamination of food, clean equipment, clean utensils, and single-service and single-use articles.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook was getting ready to put on a pair of gloves to work with portions of fried chicken without first washing their hands. Cook was eating lunch just prior to this and was advised on handwashing between tasks. Hands were washed prior to putting on gloves to handle food. Ensure hands are properly washed between tasks as needed, especially after eating/drinking and before doing anything with food.  
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed after engaging in other that contaminate hands and prior to putting on gloves.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Four separate portions of eggrolls in the walk-in cooler were observed with internal temperatures of 70F; 68F; 70F; and 81F. Three portions at 70F and 68F were in slotted storage baskets, and the last batch at 81F was in a plastic tub. Eggrolls were prepared in the early afternoon and approaching the end of the first two hours for cooling. Temperatures were checked around 3:20pm. PIC was asked to move eggrolls to the walk-in freezer to speed up cooling process. Approximately an hour later the eggrolls remained in the walk-in cooler, and the batch that was at 81F had an internal temperature of 74F. Eggrolls were past the first two hours of cooling process. Eggrolls were re-fried and reached internal temperatures above 170F. Time control was going to be used, and eggrolls would be used within less than 4hrs for dinner orders. Any leftover portions at the end of the night from this batch were too be discarded.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 1. Five batches of fried chicken portions were observed in colander bowls on the back prep table. Surface temperatures were observed at 69F-122F depending on when portions were fried. Internal temperatures were observed at 74F, 84F, 95F, 106F, and 124F. Based on information provided the chicken portions were fried recently and within the first two hours of the cooling process. Fried chicken portions were placed in plastic tubs and moved to the walk-in cooler. Temperatures were checked around 4:30pm and observed between 48F and 58F.  
2. Four separate portions of eggrolls in the walk-in cooler were observed with internal temperatures of 70F; 68F; 70F; and 81F. Three portions at 70F and 68F were in slotted storage baskets, and the last batch at 81F was in a plastic tub. Eggrolls were prepared in the early afternoon and approaching the end of the first two hours for cooling. Temperatures were checked around 3:20pm. PIC was asked to move eggrolls to the walk-in freezer to speed up cooling process. Approximately an hour later the eggrolls remained in the walk-in cooler. The three portions at 70F and 68F originally were still above 60F and moved to the walk-in freezer to help aid in quick chilling.
3. Cooked lo mein noodles in the walk-in cooler were observed with internal temperatures of 61F and 64F. Noodles were packed full to the top in two plastic containers. Noodles were prepared around noontime and were within the last four hours of cooling. Noodles were separated so product was in four tubs instead of two. PIC was asked to place noodles in the walk-in freezer to speed up the cooling process, but the portions were left in the walk-in cooler covered and stacked. Portions were at 52F-54F when checked around 4:20pm. Noodles were moved to the walk-in freezer to finish cooling.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.
When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be: (1) Arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination as specified under Subparagraph 3-305.11(A)(2), during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 PIC did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to handle food and prepare an order. Prior to putting on gloves PIC was attempting to look up information about their allergen certification on an electronic device. Handwashing between tasks and prior to putting on gloves were discussed. Gloves were discarded and hands were washed prior to putting on a new pair of gloves to continue with preparation.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed after engaging in other that contaminate hands and prior to putting on gloves.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Egg drop soup in the walk-in cooler was observed with a surface temperature of 112F and internal temperature of 122F. Soup was made for an order around 1pm and held at room until it was placed in the walk-in cooler prior to inspector’s arrival at 3pm. Based on information provided, soup was in the process of cooling for over 2 hours at the time of inspection. Soup was placed in the food warmer on the highest setting to reheat to 165F.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 Bleach available for use did not have an EPA registration number on the label. Labeling requirements for bleach were discussed. A new bottle of bleach with an EPA registration number was purchased and provided for use during inspection.
Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Bleach solution in kitchen sani-bucket was observed at proper concentration, but the water was soiled from use. Fresh sanitizer solution was prepared at 100ppm.
Chemical sanitizing solutions in which wet wiping cloths are held between uses shall be free of food debris and visible soil. Ensure sanitizer solution is changed as needed throughout the day once the solution becomes soiled and/or the concentration weakens.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 PIC was unable to locate a copy of their allergen certification. Certification may have accidentally been disposed of with other shredded documentation. Information for allergen courses was provided. Provide proof of allergen certification by the next routine inspection. 
All certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Ladle at the front service area was soiled. PIC noted it was not used during the current day of operation. Ladle was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
--Bowl used with raw egg during lunch service was observed on the counter by the prep cooler. Bowl was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that bowls and utensils used with raw animal foods are switched out up to every 4hrs and that soiled items are set aside to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Garlic in oil was observed at 84F on the cook line.  Garlic and oil mixture currently in use was removed from cold holding around 12:40pm. The portion of garlic and oil will be used or discarded by 4:40pm. Time control policy was updated to include garlic in oil mixture (see general comments for additional information).
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Portions of fried tofu in the walkin cooler and other prepared foods were without date marks. Options for date marking were discussed, including using a calendar to write down items on dates of preparation. Foods were dated during inspection. 
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (such as cooked noodles, eggrolls, fried chicken, etc.) or after original packaging is opened (such as tofu) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.citation_text:
3-501.19 Lo Mein noodles are one of the foods included in the time control policy. A portion of noodles that were out for lunch service prior to inspector's arrival were observed in the bottom of the prep cooler. The internal temperature was observed at 57F. Lo Mein was said to have been initially removed from the cooler at 1:20pm based on the time of a recent food order. The noodles were to be used or discarded by 5:20pm. Owners were advised to label noodles with time and to cease the practice of placing noodles back in the cooler once they have been out at room temperature. 
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours the food shall be cooked and served or discarde within 4 hours from the point in time when the food was removed from temperature control. Time controlled foods should not be placed back in the cooler once they are in use and held at room temperature.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing sign was missing from the handsink at the front counter. Owner noted the sign got dirty and was removed. Handwashing sign was provided and posted. Extra signs were provided to replace signage as it becomes soiled and worn over time. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees. Ensure handwashing signage is always maintained at all handsinks.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Fried sweet and sour chicken pieces were cooling in three large plastic tubs in the walkin cooler. Surface and internal temperatures were observed at 56F and 71F-73F respectively. Based on information provided the food was cooked at ~11:30am, and cooling began around maybe 12pm. Time and temperature were not being monitored to know when the chicken reached 135F to know exactly when 6hr time frame began. However, owner was given benefit of the doubt that the chicken was possibly still within the first two hours for cooling. Chicken was rotated within tubs and placed in the walkin freezer to help speed up the cooling process. 
Options for rapid chilling were discussed, including placing cooked foods in smaller portions to help chill foods quickly in the walkin freezer prior to combining in larger tubs for storage.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Tubs containing cooked lo mein noodles and fried sweet and sour chicken prepared during previous days of operation were not date marked in the walkin cooler. Both products were made within the last three days. Options for date marking were discussed. Owner was advised on use of the wall calendar hanging up front. Owner intends to begin tracking dates for prepared foods on the calendar for ease in reference. 
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (such as cooked noodles, eggrolls, fried chicken, etc.) or after original packaging is opened (such as tofu) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Cooked lo mein noodles were cooling in two tubs in the walkin cooler. Surface and internal temperatures were at 65F and 80F-82F respectively. Noodles were cooked within the last hour and a half based on information provided and were still in the first two hours of cooling process. Noodles were stirred and placed in walkin freezer to help speed up the cooling process.
Ensure time and temperature are monitored during cooling process to verify foods are reaching benchmark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling.  Use a clean, calibrated food thermometer to check temperatures frequently during cooling process.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.
When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be: (1) Arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination as specified under Subparagraph 3-305.11(A)(2), during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Sanitizer solution in kitchen sani-bucket was observed at 200ppm chlorine, but the water was cloudy and contained food debris. Fresh sanitizer solution was prepared. 
Chemical sanitizing solutions in which wet wiping cloths are held between uses shall be free of food debris and visible soil. Ensure sanitizer solution is changed as needed throughout the day once the solution becomes soiled and/or the concentration weakens.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Upon arrival PIC with CFM was not present and two other employees were present and beginning prep for the day. PIC arrived a very short time after inspector arrived. PIC stated she is typically at the facility daily by 10am but was working on a personal matter for the family prior to arrival today. PIC and staff were advised that a CFM is to be present during all hours of operation (see general comments for details).
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Evidence was observed to indicate the front handsink was used for a purpose other than handwashing. Food debris was observed in the removable portion of the drain. PIC stated the food debris could be from her children rinsing personal plates. PIC cleaned the handsink and was advised to speak with all family and staff about proper use of handsinks. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using handsinks for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15 Cans of oyster flavored sauce (2), Hoisin sauce (1), and thin soy sauce (2) were observed to be severely dented along seams or other surfaces. Cans in question were set aside and would not be used. Owners noted the supplier will not take individual cans back for returns. PIC was advised to have a designated area for storage of damaged and questionable cans until a full case of product is available for returns.
Food packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the food is not exposed to adulteration or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-304.11 Soiled tongs left from close of business Sunday were used during inspection. Tongs were removed from cook line and placed at 3 part sink for ware washing. Clean tongs were provided. Ensure all utensils and food contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitized as needed throughout each operating day and prior to use the next business day. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Cooked, cooled eggrolls were uncovered in the walkin cooler. Provide a cover for containers of eggrolls for long-term storage once food has properly cooled.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Food thermometer was observed to be soiled with grease and general buildup. Thermometer was to be cleaned and sanitized prior to use.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If bleach solution is used between temperature checks, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

Rice scoops and holder as well as fry baskets were left soiled from Sunday service. Rice scoops and holder were set aside for cleaning. Clean and sanitize rice scoops and holder up to every 4hrs after continuous use. Fry baskets need to be cleaned and sanitized at the end of operations daily.
Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use or any time contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Leftover rice cooked on Sunday was not date marked in the walkin cooler. Open package of tofu was without a date mark in the bottom of the prep cooler. Rice was to be reheated for service and tofu was date marked. 
Multiple containers of fried chicken pieces were in the walkin cooler, but only one container had a date mark. All chicken was prepared the day prior. Options for date marking multiple containers of same product with one label in the walkin cooler was discussed. For example, if three containers of fried chicken pieces are prepared the same day, owner was advised to provide one label with the date and indicate 3 containers have that date on the label.  
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Frozen shrimp was in the process of thawing in the large prep sink. A small stream of cold water was running over part of the shrimp which were held in a colander. Shrimp were placed in a metal bowl and cold water was turned on to allow for a heavier flow of water over thawing product. 
If time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food is thawed under cold running water it must meet the requirements of FDA Food Code Section 3-501.13(B), and product needs to be completely submerged during the thawing process.  
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-302.12 Metal stem food thermometer was retrieved from the reach-in cooler when PIC was asked about having a food thermometer. Staff could not find the case for the thermometer, and PIC kept the thermometer in the cooler so it didn't get lost. PIC also stated the thermometer is just used for checking temperature in the cooler and not placed directly in the food. PIC was advised the food thermometer needs to be maintained clean and calibrated and used for monitoring food temperatures during cooking, cooling, and reheating as well as to confirm proper hot and cold holding temperatures if warmers or coolers appear to be having an issue.
Food thermometer was checked with ice water and observed to be calibrated. Cleaning and maintenance of thermometer were discussed. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Portions of  unpackaged food were observed in plastic grocery sacks for carry out orders in the walkin cooler. Although sacks are single service articles they are not intended for food storage in direct contact with unpackaged and prepared foods. Use only food grade containers and bags, such as plastic food storage bags, for storage of unpackaged and prepared foods. 
FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-803.11 Slightly damp wiping cloth was observed on the ledge by the front handsink. PIC thought it may have been left by a private party that used the facility the evening prior but stated it was a clean cloth. Exact use of the wiping cloth from the evening prior was unknown and assumed to be soiled. Wiping cloth was placed in the soiled linen container upon request of inspector. 
Ensure fresh wiping cloths are used each day and soiled wiping cloths are placed in proper storage container after use.
Soiled linens shall be kept in clean, nonabsorbent receptacles or clean, washable laundry bags. Store soiled wiping cloths in the storage container when no longer needed.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-201.11 Pots of rice warmers were starting to show signs of wear. A replacement pot was available for the white rice warmer. Another replacement pot is needed for the fried rice warmer. 
Equipment and utensils shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11 A sanitizer solution was not available for use upon arrival of inspector and prep was occurring. Bleach solution was prepared upon arrival of PIC. Ensure sanitizer solution is prepared prior to beginning prep for the day and replaced throughout the day as needed. 
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text:
4-603.12 & 4-901.11 Pans were stacked in the clean storage area and observed with food debris as well as moisture on inner surfaces. Pans were removed from storage area to go through ware washing process again. PIC was advised on precleaning and repeating steps of ware washing as well as allowing pans to air dry prior to stacking in clean storage area.
If necessary for effective cleaning, utensils and equipment shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives. **Repeat soaking, precleaning, and wash/rinse/sanitize process as many times as necessary to ensure removal of soil from all surfaces.**
After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining as specified in the first paragraph of 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), before contact with food.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towel dispenser in men's restroom was empty. Paper towels were provided during inspection.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Washed, peeled onions were observed uncovered in the walkin cooler. Onions were stored under a soiled shelf. Onions were covered during inspection. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Lo mein noodles in the bottom of the prep cooler had surface and internal temperatures at 49F and 55F respectively. PIC noted the product was sitting out during lunch service since ~130pm and was placed in the cooler once inspector arrived. Owner was advised to do time control with the noodles and use or discard within 4hrs. Cease the practice of sitting food out at room temperature and then placing it back in the cooler. Cooked lo mein noodles were added to time control policy during inspection.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Cooked foods in the walkin cooler were not dated. Fried chicken portions for sweet and sour chicken, General Tso chicken, and cooked lo mein noodles were all prepared the Sunday prior. Proper dating of prepared foods was discussed, and date marks were provided. 
Refrigerated, ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety food and held in food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature 41F/below for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Plastic grocery sack for carry out orders was observed lining a pan of food in the reach-in cooler. Pan was removed to allow for proper storage. Although the sack is a single serivce article it is not intended for food storage in direct contact with unpackaged and prepared foods. Use only food grade containers and bags, such as plastic food storage bags, for storage of unpackaged and prepared foods. 
FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the ledge of the counter by the front handsink upon arrival of inspector. PIC placed wiping cloth in sanitizer for proper storage. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Walkin cooler shelving was observed with varying amounts of debris accumulation. Clean the walkin shelves as needed to eliminate buildup.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12 Operator was observed washing hands without proper technique at the front handsink. Faucet was shut off prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed, and operator was advised to reference proper handwashing posters located at handsinks for reference.
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Employee was observed rinsing hands at the 3 part sink after working with raw chicken. Operator was advised that proper handwashing is to always occur at a designated handsink. Employee washed his hands at the kitchen handsink proper to next task. 
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Baskets of cooked, cooled eggrolls were uncovered in the walkin cooler. Operator was advised to provide covers once eggrolls are finished cooling and prior to long-term storage.
Bottle of tomato color was without a lid in the dry storage area. Product was removed from dry storage for discard.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Bleach solutions just made prior to inspector's arrival were at 0ppm and less than 10ppm. The issue with concentration was likely due to the type of bleach being used (see #28 for details). Solutions were remade with correct bleach at proper concentration and observed at 150ppm.
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain bleach solutions at 150ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Scoop in bulk corn starch bin was observed with buildup on it, especially around the handle. Scoop was removed for cleaning.  General buildup of debris was also observed on the upper portion inside another bulk powder. Cleaning frequency for bulk storage containers was discussed.
Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be cleaned any time contamination may have occurred or up to every 24hrs depending on use.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Operators were in the process of rolling vegetable eggrolls when inspector arrived. Operators stopped working with the eggrolls as soon as the inspector arrived and left wraps and egg in bowls out on prep tables. Cracked egg was observed at 54F/63F and eggroll wraps were observed at 57F/66F after sitting out for ~1hr. Prepared eggrolls were fried and remaining product was used. Operators were advised it is a bad practice to leave foods at ambient temperature if prep is stopped for an extended period of time. Place foods back in coolers if prep is stopped for longer than a few minutes.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Cooked foods in the walkin cooler and bottom of the prep cooler did not have date marks. Foods included eggrolls, noodles, General Tso chicken, and sweet and sour chicken. All foods were cooked within the last one or two business days per information provided. Foods were labeled and kept for use. 
Refrigerated, ready to eat, TCS food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded within 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 Lemon scented Great Value brand bleach was available for use. Concentration of bleach solutions were likely effected by the type of bleach being used (see #16 for details). Proper bleach intended for sanitizing food contact surfaces was provided during the inspection. 
Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.12 Five gallon soy sauce bucket was observed under the prep sink plumbing. Soy sauce was not opened, but operator was advised it is not a good practice to store any food, regardless of packaging, under plumbing in case the plumbing would leak. Soy sauce was moved to the dry storage area. 
Food may not be stored in under anything that may be a source of contamination.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the ledge of the front counter by the handsink. Wiping cloth was placed in bleach solution for proper storage. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Debris that appeared to be small, dead flies was observed inside the open packaging that had to-go boxes in the dry storage area. Packaging and to-go boxes were discarded. 
Single service and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Cardboard was used to line shelving in storage areas and on the bottom of the rice cooker table. Some of the cardboard was soiled with general buildup and splash. A soiled cardboard box was also observed being used for storage on the shelf behind the rice cooker. Options were discussed for cleanable, plastic tubs and other re-usable materials to be used for storage and lining shelving. Start replacing the cardboard.
Nonfood-contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) walkin cooler shelves (general buildup/food debris); 
B) dry storage shelving (general buildup);  and
C) chemical storage shelves by 3 part sink (general buildup). 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.citation_text:
6-302.11 Toilet paper was not available in the women's room. Toilet paper was provided.
A supply of toilet tissue shall be available at each toilet

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-305.11 Personal items were observed sitting on bottled water packages and hanging on aprons on dry storage shelving. All items were moved to proper storage areas. 
Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 One of the employees has not obtained his food handler certification. 
All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
(R) 750.140 - Eggrolls were in the process of being fried and cooling. Eggrolls cooling on trays by the back door were observed with surface temperatures at 160°F. No time was indicated on the trays, but the process just began upon arrival of inspector. Eggrolls typically sit out for about an hour prior to being placed in the walkin cooler to finish cooling. Operator was advised on tracking the time and temperature of cooling foods.

Cooked foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Properly label cooling foods and monitor the cooling process to ensure foods cool from 135°F to 70°F/below within 2hrs and from 70°F to 41°F/below within an additional 4hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Use a clean calibrated stem thermometer to verify foods are reaching benchmark temperatures in the designated time for proper cooling.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
(R) 750.153 - Bowl of fried chicken pieces was observed on the prep table across from the fryers. Product had surface temperatures in the high forty to fifty degree Fahrenheit range. Chicken was just removed from the cooler around 1030a to make an order. Operator was advised to label with time stamp if time control was to be used, as it typically is for working supplies of fried chicken and foods in the Coke cooler. Chicken was placed in the Coke cooler and observed with a lower surface temperature a bit later. 

When using time as a control, food shall be marked to indicate the time when it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Also, if time control is used then staff must adhere to time control and not go from letting foods sit out at ambient temperature and then placing them back in the cooler. The Coke cooler doesn't always hold consistent temperatures, and the owner indicated time control would be used today when told temperatures of foods were at 43°F-44°F. Surface temperatures were later observed at 40°F-41°F. 
Indicate the time when foods are placed in the Coke cooler and when working supplies of food are removed from cold holding to use. 
Use or discard foods within 4hrs.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
(R) 750.240 - Chicken was observed in tubs with standing water at the 3 part sink upon arrival of inspector. Operator noted it was chopped frozen chicken that was in the process of thawing. Surface temperature was 57°F, while internal temperature for chicken was at 62°F. Tubs of chicken were placed under cold running water for a bit longer until operator could coat chicken with sauce prior to storage in the walkin cooler.

Foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be properly thawed by one of the following methods. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under potable running water 70°F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment:
(R) 750.120 - Cleavers were once again observed within the crevice between the prep cooler and the table next to it. One cleaver had food debris on it and had not yet been used this morning. The surface of the table where cleavers were stored had debris buildup. Utensils were removed and taken to the 3 part sink for ware washing.

Container for rice scoops was soiled with food debris in the bottom. Operator noted the scoops may not have been cleaned the evening prior. The scoops and container were removed and taken to the 3 part sink for ware washing. 

Green eggroll storage basket was observed on the bottom shelf of a prep table. the basket had stuck on grease and crumbs. Operator noted the baskets get cleaned after every couple uses. Eggroll baskets need to be cleaned and sanitized after every use just like all other food contact surface. Basket was to be cleaned and sanitized prior to next use. 

Operator noted all soiled items would be cleaned and sanitized at the 3 part sink after sinks are cleaned once raw chicken prep was finished for the day.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Properly clean and sanitize in-use food contact surfaces (e.g. cleavers, knives, cutting boards, tongs, slicer) up to every 4hrs after continuous use. Place soiled utensils and equipment at the 3 part sink for ware washing at the end of operations daily.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Open can of ketchup was observed in the bottom of the prep cooler. Operator stated it was probably opened the day prior. Operator was advised that ketchup is acidic and needs to be placed in a proper food grade container once the original #10 can is opened. Ketchup was placed in a proper container during inspection.

Foods shall be properly stored at all times. Place acidic foods in a stainless steel pan or plastic food grade storage container after the original #10 can is opened. Metals and metallic flavor can leach into the food if it is stored in the original container after it is opened.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.512 & 160 - Operators were observed putting on gloves without first washing hands and not washing hands between glove changes. Handwashing and glove use were discussed.

Food handlers must properly wash their hands before putting on gloves and between glove changes.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
(R) 750.140 - Eggrolls were in the process of being fried and cooling. Eggrolls cooling on trays by the back door were observed with surface temperatures at 120°F-160°F depending on when they were fried. No time was indicated on the trays, but the process just began within the hour prior to inspector's arrival. Eggrolls typically sit out for about an hour prior to being placed in the walkin cooler to finish cooling. Operator was advised on tracking the time and temperature of cooling foods. Eggrolls were moved into the cooler during the inspection.

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Properly label cooling foods and monitor the cooling process to ensure foods cool from 135°F to 70°F/below within 2hrs and from 70°F to 41°F/below within an additional 4hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.153 - Coke cooler was observed holding products above 41°F this morning. Owners have a time control policy posted on the cooler, but time was not indicated as to when foods were removed from the walkin cooler and placed in the Coke cooler today. Normally foods are placed in the cooler around 1030a. Today foods were placed in the Coke cooler around 930a. A piece of paper with the time stamp of 930a was placed on the cooler. All time/temperature control for safety foods (eggrolls, chicken) must be used or discarded by 130p. Owner was advised to write down the new time when foods are placed in the cooler for each batch of product. 

A tub of fried chicken pieces was also observed on a lower shelf of a prep table across from the fryers. Product had surface temperatures ranging from 37°F-43°F. Chicken in question was just removed from the walkin cooler prior to inspector's arrival. Time stamp of 1030a was placed on the tub of chicken. Fried chicken pieces will be used or discarded by 230p. 

When using time as a control, food shall be marked to indicate the time when  it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label food.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Chicken was observed in tubs with standing water at the 3 part sink upon arrival of inspector. Operator noted it was chopped frozen chicken that was in the process of thawing. Surface temperature was 60°F, while internal temperature for chicken was at 44°F. Owner noted the whole process takes less than 2hrs; once chicken is soft it is then coated with sauce prior to being placed in the walkin cooler. The tubs of chicken were placed under cold running water during the inspection prior to being strained, sauced and placed in the walkin cooler for storage

Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the following methods. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under potable running water 70°F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - A) Cleavers and a knife soiled with food debris were observed within the crevice between the prep cooler and the table next to it. Utensils were removed and taken to the 3 part sink.
B) Container for rice scoops was soiled with food debris in the bottom. Operator noted the scoops may not have been cleaned the evening prior. The scoops and container were removed and taken to the 3 part sink. A new container and clean scoop were retrieved for use.
Operator noted all soiled items would be cleaned and sanitized at the 3 part sink after sinks are cleaned once raw chicken prep was finished for the day.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Properly clean and sanitize in-use food contact surfaces (e.g. cleavers, knives, cutting boards, tongs, slicer) up to every 4hrs after continuous use. Place soiled utensils and equipment at the 3 part sink for ware washing at the end of operations daily.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Wontons in the Coke cooler and pork in the walkin freezer were stored in plastic grocery sacks. Operator noted food grade bags are available for use .Pork was placed in a proper bag before placing back in the walkin freezer. Wontons were placed in proper food grade container in the Coke cooler.

Foods shall be properly stored at all times. Use only food grade bags and containers for storage of opened and prepared foods.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Operator was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a proper barrier. Proper technique was discussed, and operator re-washed hands properly. Proper handwashing technique poster is located at all handsinks, and staff are working on making permanent corrective action to properly wash hands consistently.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
Use paper towels to dry hands and then use paper towels to shut off the faucet. If hands need to be dried further once the faucet has been shut off, then get a new paper towel to finish drying hands.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - A) Scoops in bulk powder bins had some buildup of debris around handles.
B) Slicer was observed with what appeared to be food debris on the underside beneath slicing surface.
Clean and sanitize scoops and the slicer.

Food contact surfaces must be properly cleaned and sanitized between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use for in-use utensils and equipment, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed a bowl of fried chicken on the counter top to be at 66F. This item should be time marked when the item was removed from heat control. Management stated the food had been cooling for approximately 2 hours. Facility has an additional 4 hours to get the food item below 41F. Mark the times at which items are removed from heat control. Item was placed into the refrigerator to quickly cool the food.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: CORRECTED> Observed a large bowl of chicken at the prep sink to be at 63. According to the staff, the chicken was thawed approximately 2 hours ago. Facility agreed to cook all the chicken within 2 hours to correct the violation. Make sure to properly thaw and store food that required cold holding. Handout on proper thawing practices given. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above). 750-153(a) Food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. Do not hold food in excess of four hours after removal from temperature control.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed a wet wiping cloth stored on a counter top. Make sure to store wiping cloths in sanitizer buckets between uses at proper sanitizing concentrations. Use test kits to verify sanitizer concentrations.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed garlic powder unlabeled in a container.  The container was labeled with the proper common name.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed raw chicken stored above shell eggs in walk in cooler.  Chicken was stored on bottom of walk in cooler during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-130(d)  All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed shrimp on the floor in the walk in freezer. All food must be stored at least 6" off the floor to protect the food.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed foil on the fire suppression system. Remove the foil, clean and sanitize as needed.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.comment:
Observed garlic powder to be stored in a peanut butter container.   Single service items are not to be reused in the establishment. Place spices in food grade containers and label the container.
750-600 Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed a bottle of chemical to not be labeled during the inspection.  The bottle was labeled with the contents during the inspection.
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.
